Step 4: Match reaction (S). Diazotization of aniline followed by Sandmeyer reaction with $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2/\text{HCl}$ converts the diazonium group into a chloro group, yielding chlorobenzene. Thus, $\text{S} \rightarrow 1$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Cyclohexene is treated with $N$-bromosuccinimide (NBS) in carbon tetrachloride ($\text{CCl}_4$) in the presence of light ($h\nu$) and a trace of benzoyl peroxide. What is the major organic product formed and its reaction mechanism?
options: A) 1-Bromocyclohex-1-ene via vinylic radical substitution
B) 1,2-Dibromocyclohexane via electrophilic addition across the double bond
C) 3-Bromocyclohex-1-ene via allylic free-radical bromination
D) Bromocyclohexane via free-radical addition of $\text{HBr}$
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the function of NBS. $N$-Bromosuccinimide (NBS) is a specialized reagent used for selective allylic and benzylic bromination of alkenes and alkylarenes.
Step 2: Trace the free-radical mechanism. Light initiates cleavage of the weak $\text{N}-\text{Br}$ bond in NBS to generate a bromine free radical ($\text{Br}^\bullet$). The bromine radical selectively abstracts an allylic hydrogen atom from cyclohexene because the developing cyclohexenyl radical is strongly stabilized by resonance with the adjacent carbon-carbon double bond (allylic resonance energy $\approx 50\text{ kJ/mol}$).
Step 3: Analyze product formation. NBS maintains a steady, very low concentration of molecular bromine ($\text{Br}_2$) in solution by reacting with trace $\text{HBr}$. The resonance-stabilized allylic radical reacts with $\text{Br}_2$ to yield 3-bromocyclohex-1-ene while regenerating a bromine radical. Electrophilic addition across the double bond is suppressed due to the low $\text{Br}_2$ concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Two isomeric dihaloalkanes with molecular formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Cl}_2$, Compound X and Compound Y, are subjected to alkaline hydrolysis with aqueous potassium hydroxide ($\text{aq. KOH}$):
- Compound X yields an aldehyde (ethanal) as the sole organic product.
- Compound Y yields a diol (ethane-1,2-diol) as the sole organic product.
Which of the following correctly identifies Compound X, Compound Y, and their classification?
options: A) Compound X is 1,1-dichloroethane (vicinal dihalide); Compound Y is 1,2-dichloroethane (geminal dihalide)
B) Compound X is 1,2-dichloroethane (vicinal dihalide); Compound Y is 1,1-dichloroethane (geminal dihalide)
C) Both Compound X and Compound Y are vicinal dihalides
D) Compound X is 1,1-dichloroethane (geminal dihalide); Compound Y is 1,2-dichloroethane (vicinal dihalide)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand geminal vs vicinal dihalides. In geminal dihalides (alkylidene halides), both halogen atoms are attached to the same carbon atom. In vicinal dihalides (alkylene dihalides), the two halogen atoms are attached to adjacent carbon atoms.
Step 2: Analyze hydrolysis of Compound X. In 1,1-dichloroethane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(Cl)}_2$), nucleophilic displacement of both chlorine atoms by hydroxide produces an unstable gem-diol intermediate: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}_2$. Gem-diols spontaneously lose a molecule of water to produce a carbonyl group, yielding ethanal (acetaldehyde, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$). Hence, Compound X is 1,1-dichloroethane (a geminal dihalide).
Step 3: Analyze hydrolysis of Compound Y. In 1,2-dichloroethane ($\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$), nucleophilic displacement of chlorine on each carbon by hydroxide produces a stable vicinal diol: ethane-1,2-diol (ethylene glycol, $\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$). Hence, Compound Y is 1,2-dichloroethane (a vicinal dihalide).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding organometallic reactions of haloalkanes and haloarenes:
Statement I: The reaction of phenylmagnesium bromide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}$) with propan-2-one (acetone) in dry ether followed by acidic hydrolysis produces 2-phenylpropan-2-ol as a tertiary alcohol.
Statement II: Grignard reagents add nucleophilically across the polar carbonyl double bond ($\text{C}^{\delta+}=\text{O}^{\delta-}$), wherein the nucleophilic carbon atom of the alkyl/aryl group attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon while the magnesium atom coordinates to the carbonyl oxygen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. The reaction of a ketone with a Grignard reagent yields a tertiary alcohol upon hydrolysis. Specifically, addition of phenylmagnesium bromide to acetone ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{O}$) produces a magnesium alkoxide adduct ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)-\text{OMgBr}$), which upon acidification with dilute $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ hydrolyzes to 2-phenylpropan-2-ol: $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{OH}$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The carbon-magnesium bond in Grignard reagents is strongly polarized ($C^{\delta-} - \text{Mg}^{\delta+}$). The carbonyl carbon of the ketone is electron-deficient due to electronegativity of oxygen ($C^{\delta+} = \text{O}^{\delta-}$). The nucleophilic aryl/alkyl carbanion attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon, forming a new carbon-carbon bond, while the electropositive $-\text{MgX}$ group coordinates to oxygen to form a halo-magnesium alkoxide complex. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When $(2E)$-but-2-ene and $(2Z)$-but-2-ene are treated separately with bromine in carbon tetrachloride ($\text{Br}_2/\text{CCl}_4$) in the dark, what are the stereochemical configurations of the 2,3-dibromobutane products obtained from the $(E)$ and $(Z)$ isomers, respectively?
options: A) $(2E)$-but-2-ene gives a racemic $(\pm)$-mixture, while $(2Z)$-but-2-ene gives $meso$-2,3-dibromobutane
B) $(2E)$-but-2-ene gives $meso$-2,3-dibromobutane, while $(2Z)$-but-2-ene gives a racemic $(\pm)$-mixture of $(2R,3R)$- and $(2S,3S)$-2,3-dibromobutane
C) Both $(2E)$- and $(2Z)$-but-2-ene yield $meso$-2,3-dibromobutane exclusively
D) Both $(2E)$- and $(2Z)$-but-2-ene yield a racemic $(\pm)$-mixture exclusively
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the stereochemical mechanism of electrophilic bromination of alkenes. The addition of bromine ($\text{Br}_2$) to alkenes is a stereospecific anti-addition proceeding through a cyclic bromonium ion intermediate followed by backside nucleophilic attack of bromide ($\text{Br}^-$).
Step 2: Apply anti-addition to $(E)$-but-2-ene (trans isomer). Anti-addition of two identical halogen atoms across a symmetrical trans alkene ($E$-alkene) creates a molecule with an internal plane of symmetry. Attack of bromide on either carbon of the cyclic bromonium ion produces identical structures that are superimposable on their mirror images, yielding the optically inactive $meso$-2,3-dibromobutane.
Step 3: Apply anti-addition to $(Z)$-but-2-ene (cis isomer). Anti-addition across a symmetrical cis alkene ($Z$-alkene) produces a chiral product lacking any internal symmetry plane. Backside attack on the two bridgehead carbons occurs with equal probability, generating an equimolar ($1:1$) pair of enantiomers: $(2R,3R)$-2,3-dibromobutane and $(2S,3S)$-2,3-dibromobutane (a racemic mixture).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following comprehensive reaction sequence involving haloalkane and polyhalogen chemistry:
$$\text{Ethanol} \xrightarrow{\text{PCl}_5} \text{A} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN (alc.)}} \text{B} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \Delta} \text{C} \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_3, \Delta} \text{D} \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2 / \text{aq. KOH}} \text{E} \xrightarrow{\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{alc. KOH}, \Delta} \text{F}$$
What is the structure and characteristic property of Compound F?
options: A) Ethyl cyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$), an odourless crystalline solid
B) Propyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NC}$), having a fruity ester-like fragrance
C) Ethyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC}$), having an extremely intolerable and foul odour
D) Methyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{NC}$), a sweet-smelling gas
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify Compound A. Reaction of ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) with $\text{PCl}_5$ yields chloroethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$).
Step 2: Identify Compound B and C. Nucleophilic substitution of chloroethane with alcoholic $\text{KCN}$ yields propanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$, Compound B). Complete acidic hydrolysis of the nitrile yields propanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, Compound C).
Step 3: Identify Compound D and E. Reaction of propanoic acid with ammonia followed by strong heating yields propanamide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$, Compound D). Treatment of propanamide with bromine and aqueous $\text{KOH}$ is the Hoffmann bromamide degradation, which degrades the carbon chain by one carbon to produce ethanamine (ethylamine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, Compound E).
Step 4: Identify Compound F. Reaction of primary amine ethanamine with chloroform and alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ is the carbylamine test (isocyanide test): $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 + \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{KOH} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC} + 3\text{KCl} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Compound F is ethyl isocyanide (ethyl carbylamine), famous for its extremely foul and repulsive odor.
